title: MandatePatch
description: §4. 'A single-use modification of the scope of a payment authorization for one transaction; equivalently, a transaction-specific amendment of a stored mandate, or a delta authorization' (§9 vocabulary). §4.1: 'a structured delta against an immutable, still-live base: an object that identifies which predicate or predicates of a persistent signed mandate were violated, records the human's amended value for each, binds to exactly one checkout and to the suspended execution state that produced it, is consumed on use, and — the load-bearing property — never propagates, so that sibling and future transactions under the same mandate resolve against the unpatched base.' §4.1: 'A MandatePatch is ephemeral by construction. Durable change is exclusively Section 5 supersession.' Fields below mirror §4.2 one for one; none are added and none are omitted.

base_mandate_hash.description: §4.2, 'the mandate version being patched'. Hash of the specific mandate version, not the family: §5.1 states that 'supersession voids unconsumed patches against superseded versions'. §4.2: 'Patch-of-patch is prohibited' — this field MUST reference a mandate, never another MandatePatch.

patch_sequence.description: §4.2, 'monotonic within the mandate'. §4.4: 'After a low, profile-defined mandatory number of patches, supersession is forced.' §6.2: 'the patch sequence number and a per-checkout distinguisher [are] displayed' in the challenge rendering. PROFILE-DEFINED: the forced-supersession ceiling ('a low, profile-defined mandatory number').

violations.description: §4.2, 'one or more (violated_predicate_id, value_old, value_new) tuples, all covered by the single human_signature below'. §4.2: 'To prevent serial suspension fatigue, the evaluating wallet, gateway, or attested scorer MUST surface every failing predicate in the initial suspension, so that a single challenge and a single signature can cover the full tuple set.' §4.2: 'A patch waives nothing except the predicates it names, to exactly the values it names.' §4.2: 'Patches amend only principal-owned predicates: where an issuer, lender, or program has pinned a predicate — a covenant, an eligibility rule, a category restriction — that predicate is unpatchable by the principal, and a MandatePatch cannot make a transaction permissible that a third party's independent policy prohibits.'

violated_predicate_id.description: §4.2. Identifier of the violated predicate in the base mandate's predicate set. MUST name a principal-owned, patchable predicate (§4.2); a third-party-pinned predicate is unpatchable and 'failure of an unpatchable third-party predicate declines'.

value_old.description: §4.2, 'value_old committed or disclosed per policy'. Either the disclosed prior value (any JSON value) or a commitment to it. PROFILE-DEFINED: the disclosure policy and the commitment scheme used when `value_old` is committed rather than disclosed.

value_new.description: §4.2. 'records the human's amended value' for the named predicate (§4.1). For a semantic violation: §4.2, 'the tuple's value_new encodes the set of approved line-item identifiers within the canonical commitment — approval of those exact flagged lines, with whole-cart approval as the degenerate all-lines case; a per-checkout threshold override is expressly not a permitted encoding, both because it leaks scoring information and because it authorizes a boundary rather than a decision.' A verifier MUST reject a `value_new` that encodes a threshold, score, or scoring-stack substitution for a semantic predicate.

checkout_commitment.description: §4.2, 'the Section 4.3 canonical commitment'. §4.2: 'A verifier honors a patch only for a transaction whose canonical commitment matches checkout_commitment.' §4.2: 'If resolving the drift changes the cart, the changed cart is a new canonical commitment requiring fresh evaluation from the beginning: a patch never authorizes a moving target.' §6.1: where a challenge presented several candidates, 'the human's signature selects exactly one, the resulting MandatePatch binds that candidate's commitment, unselected candidates are void'.

suspended_state_hash.description: §4.2, 'binds to the paused agent execution state'. §6.1: 'the human's signature is simultaneously the MandatePatch signature and a resumption credential cryptographically bound to suspended_state_hash, so the agent resumes only into the exact paused execution, only with amended scope, and only for the identified checkout.'

divergence_record_ref.description: §4.2, 'the Section 3 signed record for the bound candidate's commitment (for the original cart, the triggering record)'. §3.1: 'every evaluation emits a signed divergence record — score commitment, stack measurement, threshold, and outcome — appended to the mandate's lineage'. §4.4: 'The patch together with its divergence record forms the dispute-evidence bundle.'

nonce.description: §4.2, 'nonce single-use per mandate family ... all three enter the signed transcript'. The patch 'is consumed on use' (§4.1) and 'is nullified at the consume authority (Section 5.3) upon authorization' (§4.2); §5.3: 'Exactly-once patch consumption across heterogeneous rails is achieved by construction at that authority, not assumed of the rails.' PROFILE-DEFINED: nonce length and encoding, and the nullifier derivation — §7 specifies it is 'domain-separated over issuer, mandate family, version, patch sequence, checkout, rail, and purpose'.

issued_at.description: §4.2, 'all three enter the signed transcript'. Issuance instant of the patch.

expiry.description: §4.2, 'expiry anchored to issued_at per profile TTL; all three enter the signed transcript'. §6.1: 'fail-closed expiry: an expired challenge voids the checkout; nothing silently proceeds or falls back.' PROFILE-DEFINED: the TTL by which `expiry` is anchored to `issued_at`.

render_state_hash.description: §4.2, 'optional; Section 6.3 presentation-state attestation'. §6.3: 'Mandate and MandatePatch signatures optionally carry a render-state hash computed over the composited interface as presented, above the deterministic text rendering: pinned font hash, locale-fixed numeric formatting within that font, no truncation of operative fields, and images excluded from operative regions or bound through required alternative text.' §6.3 also states the limit: the claim is 'evidence of presentation and of the user's confirmation action — never proof of informed consent'. PROFILE-DEFINED: the composited-interface canonicalization over which this hash is computed.

attestation_tier.description: §4.2, 'optional; hardware / OS-composited / software, per Section 6.3'. §6.3: 'a tiered attestation level (hardware secure-display, OS-composited, software) is recorded in the artifact, with the software tier declared evidentially weak'.

human_signature.description: §4.2, 'authenticator-bound; domain-separated per Section 6'. §6.1: the response is dual-purpose — 'simultaneously the MandatePatch signature and a resumption credential cryptographically bound to suspended_state_hash'. §6.2: 'The signed transcript is domain-separated over audience, relying party, mandate family and version, rail, and protocol purpose, so an honestly-signed response transplanted into another accepting context fails verification.'

$comment: Constraints from §4.2 that JSON Schema cannot express, recorded here and in field descriptions so that no implementer has to reread the paper to find them: (1) 'Patch-of-patch is prohibited' — base_mandate_hash MUST resolve to a mandate, never to a MandatePatch. (2) 'Authorization under a patch is a full de novo evaluation of the entire predicate set — machine-enforceable constraints, every third-party-pinned predicate, the semantic gate over every line item, cumulative budgets, and the Section 5.2 freshness check — against the canonical commitment under the base mandate as modified by the patch.' (3) 'a transaction that satisfies its patched predicates but fails another patchable, principal-owned predicate is suspended again; failure of an unpatchable third-party predicate declines.' (4) 'a per-checkout threshold override is expressly not a permitted encoding.' (5) §4.4: 'While any patch is pending — the pending state beginning at challenge issuance and ending at patch consumption, challenge expiry, or decline — the base mandate is locked against new authorization requests at the consume authority.' (6) §5.1: 'supersession voids unconsumed patches against superseded versions.' Enforcement of all six is the verifier's and the consume authority's job and is deliberately out of scope for this repository, which ships artifacts only.

anchor.description: Independent evidence that a signature existed at its `signed_at`. OPTIONAL but RECOMMENDED: routine verification can rely on a self-asserted `signed_at`, but dispute-grade evidence cannot, because a self-asserted timestamp is asserted by the one party with an incentive to misstate it. PROFILE-DEFINED: profile v1 anchors into the §5.2 transparency log rather than standing up a second log — §5.2 already requires 'cosigned heads or a witness network against split-view equivocation', which is precisely the property a time anchor needs, so reusing it adds a guarantee without adding an operator. RECORDED ALTERNATIVE: an RFC 3161 timestamp authority, which a §5.2 issuer-registry deployment needs instead, since such a deployment may run no log at all. Stapled at signing time, so dispute-time verification never depends on a service endpoint still being reachable years later.

log_id.description: Identifier of the §5.2 transparency log this signature is anchored in.

epoch.description: Log epoch whose cosigned head covers this entry — the same epoch space a supersession record advances (§5.2, §7).

inclusion_proof.description: Merkle audit path from this signature's leaf to the epoch head, ordered leaf-ward to root-ward, each sibling hash base64url unpadded. PROFILE-DEFINED: leaf encoding and the log's hash function.

hash.description: PROFILE-DEFINED hash encoding. Profile v1: SHA-256 over the JCS (RFC 8785) serialization of the object, base64url without padding, prefixed with the algorithm name.

kid.description: Key identifier of the signing key. PROFILE-DEFINED: the derivation. Profile v1 uses `base64url(SHA-256(SPKI DER))` without padding — the unpadded base64url encoding of the SHA-256 digest of the DER-encoded SubjectPublicKeyInfo of the signing public key. The identifier is therefore CONTENT-DERIVED and unambiguous without consulting any directory; a key directory only RESOLVES a `kid` to its material and validity interval, it never defines it. REQUIRED, and deliberately not optional: evidence signed without a key identifier is verifiable only by trial-verification against every historical key, which goes ambiguous the instant two keys coexist. This field is NOT retrofittable — artifacts already signed without it can never be cleanly verified after a rotation, which is why it is present from the first commit. RECORDED ALTERNATIVE: an RFC 7638 JWK thumbprint, which is equally content-derived but fixes the key representation to JWK rather than SPKI.

alg.description: Signature algorithm identifier, JOSE/COSE name. PROFILE-DEFINED: the disclosure constrains no algorithm suite. Profile v1 admits exactly this set — ES256/ES384/ES512, the ECDSA suite AP2 v0.2 requires of its bindings; EdDSA (Ed25519); and RS256/PS256, which appear on deployed WebAuthn authenticators. A binding profile MAY narrow this enum but MUST NOT widen it without taking a new profile identifier. This member REPLACES the former free-string `algorithm`: a free string and a constrained identifier naming the same fact can disagree, and disagreement about the algorithm is disagreement about what the signature covers.

signed_at.description: The signing instant, RFC 3339 with 'Z' and second precision — the same timestamp form every other timestamp in this repository uses (PROFILE-DEFINED, decided; profile v1 takes no epoch-integer form, so that a validity interval and an artifact's `issued_at`/`expiry` are always directly comparable). This is the instant that key-validity intervals are evaluated AGAINST: a signature verifies iff `signed_at` falls inside the [not_before, not_after] interval recorded for `kid`, and a verifier MUST verify against THE KEY CURRENT AT SIGNING TIME, NEVER THE KEY CURRENT NOW. Rejecting evidence because its signing key was rotated afterwards is a bug, not a security property — planned retirement is prospective only, and evidence anchored before it stays valid permanently. A self-asserted `signed_at` is adequate for routine verification and NOT adequate for dispute-grade evidence; see `anchor`.

authenticator.description: §6.2: 'Authenticator requirements are expressed as assurance profiles — named tiers of authenticator strength and channel independence that a mandate or verifier policy selects by risk. High-risk patches require device-bound credentials or an authenticator independent of the ecosystem controlling the agent session; a registered passkey is the floor, not the profile.'

credential_id.description: Identifier of the authenticator credential that produced the signature.

channel_independent.description: §6.2, §8. Whether the authenticator is 'independent of the ecosystem controlling the agent session'. §8: 'Channel non-independence — an authenticator controlled by the same ecosystem as the agent session — is addressed by assurance profiles, not assumed away.'

assurance_profile.description: §6.2. Named assurance tier selected by mandate or verifier policy. PROFILE-DEFINED: the tier vocabulary.

domain_separation.description: §6.2: 'The signed transcript is domain-separated over audience, relying party, mandate family and version, rail, and protocol purpose.'

purpose.description: §6.2, 'protocol purpose'. For a MandatePatch the purpose is dual (§6.1): delta authorization and resumption credential.

ds_tag.description: §6.2 domain-separation tag: the digest of the domain separator this signature is bound to, base64url unpadded. DISPOSITION (PROFILE-DEFINED, DECIDED — this is the choice the schema makes rather than leaves implicit): profile v1 carries `ds_tag` HERE, in the JSON body, beside the `domain_separation` components it is derived from, AND requires it to byte-equal the domain separator bound into the carrier's signed input — the WebAuthn `clientDataJSON.challenge`, or the KB-JWT `aud`/`nonce` under an SD-JWT binding. A verifier MUST recompute the tag from `domain_separation` and MUST compare it against the value bound in the carrier; a body `ds_tag` not reproduced in the carrier is NOT covered by the signature and MUST be rejected. The body copy exists so that evidence can be checked offline without a carrier parser; the carrier copy is what makes the separator signature-covered. Leaving this disposition implicit is exactly what §6.2's transplant attack needs in order to succeed, because two verifiers would otherwise disagree about whether the separator is signature-covered at all. RECORDED ALTERNATIVE: carry the tag ENTIRELY in the WebAuthn/KB-JWT layer and leave only the components in the body — rejected for v1 because it makes offline evidence verification depend on a carrier parser, and because body components carrying no tag invite a verifier to treat them as authoritative when nothing signs them. PROFILE-DEFINED derivation, profile v1: SHA-256 over the ASCII prefix 'MandateLifecycle/v1/transcript' followed by LP(purpose), LP(audience), LP(relying_party), LP(mandate_family_id), LP(decimal encoding of mandate_version), LP(rail), LP(binding_profile), where LP(x) is the uint16 big-endian byte length of the UTF-8 encoding of x followed by those bytes — length-prefixed with NO delimiters, because `relying_party` and `mandate_family_id` are attacker-influenced. The prefix MUST differ from the §7 nullifier prefix ('MandateLifecycle/v1/nullifier') so that a transcript tag and a nullifier tag can never collide.

anchor.description: OPTIONAL but RECOMMENDED — see the `$defs/anchor` description. Omit it and `signed_at` is self-asserted, which does not carry dispute-grade weight, because the signer is precisely the party with an incentive to misstate the signing time.

signature.description: Detached signature over the domain-separated signed transcript, base64url without padding. PROFILE-DEFINED: the exact transcript construction.
